messages:
Dave (Acme): Hey team — running into a nasty one. We call two tools in parallel (search + summarize) but responses sometimes get swapped and our app shows summaries for the wrong search. Also billing shows tokens attributed to the summarize tool for requests that obviously hit search. Happening 3x today. Correlation: r-9f3b.
Alice (Support): Sorry — that sounds bad. Can you paste a minimal request + the raw response you got? Any headers (trace-id / x-request-trace)?
Dave (Acme): Here's a tiny repro (sanitized). We call /v1/call with payload:```json
{
  "model":"gpt-...",
  "tools":[{"name":"search","call_id":"A1"},{"name":"summarize","call_id":"B1"}],
  "fanout": true,
  "prompt": "..."
}```Response we got:```json
{
  "id":"resp-xxx",
  "tool_results":[{"call_id":"B1","output":"<search results>"},{"call_id":"A1","output":"<summary>"}]
}```So outputs are paired to the wrong call_id.
Alice (Support): Thanks — that's super helpful. I need the full HTTP headers if possible (x-request-trace, authorization masked ok) and the raw gateway logs. Carmen, can you take a look? Seems like a fanout/correlation mapping problem.
Carmen (Eng): On it. Quick questions: 1) Are you using any custom call_id mapping on client side? 2) Can you confirm if you set wait_for_tool_results / sequential flags?
Dave (Acme): No custom mapping. We just set fanout: true. We don't set sequential. 100% reproducible for us with concurrency 2-4.
Carmen (Eng): Noted. Ben — any deploys near that time? Could be a routing change in tool-router.
Ben (Oncall): deploy-bot posted a canary earlier:
deploy-bot: deployed tool-router v2.14.0 to canary at 1728129800 by ci/cd (notes: "improve fanout jitter, fix routing cache").
Carmen (Eng): Hmm. v2.14 touched correlation key handling. I want the gateway traces. Dave, can you resend one failing request with header `X-Request-Trace: r-9f3b` and set `X-Debug-Mode: tool-trace`? We'll pull the spans.
Dave (Acme): Sent — same timestamp, trace r-9f3b. Attached shortened logs:```
[gateway] req_id=r-9f3b fanout=2 -> router fanout_ids=[fa,fb]
[router] mapping: fa -> search (call_id A1), fb -> summarize (call_id B1)
[router] returned results list: [res_fb, res_fa]
[gateway] assemble: iterate results in return order, attach to call_ids by index => attaches res_fb to A1, res_fa to B1
```So looks like gateway assumes result ordering matches original tools order and attaches by index. If router returns in different order assembly breaks.
Carmen (Eng): That's the smoking gun — gateway should use explicit result.call_id mapping, not index order. I see in the 2.14 change we optimized for "preserveOrder" in the happy path but didn't handle out-of-order router responses. Potential bug.
Elaine (QA): Workaround for customers: set `fanout: { preserve_order: true }` or set `sequential: true` in the request to force ordered execution. Also we can add a server-side mitigation to prefer result.call_id when present.
Alice (Support): Dave — can you test with preserve_order:true and confirm?
Dave (Acme): Tried preserve_order: true — reproducible less often, but still saw one mismatch. sequential:true fixes it (no mismatches), but that's not acceptable for our latencies.
Carmen (Eng): Ok. I'll open a PR to change gateway assembly to always prefer explicit result.call_id mapping when present. That will be a quick fix. ETA for patch: ~2h testing + canary.
Ben (Oncall): Given deploy-bot canary at 1728129800, I'll hold the v2.14 rollout and revert canary if we see more. For now, recommend customers set sequential or preserve_order.
Alice (Support): Also flagging billing: because output mapping is wrong, some token usage was billed to wrong tool ids (summarize vs search). I've cc'd Billing Ops. Dave — can you export the invoices/usage windows for the correlated requests so Billing can reconcile?
Dave (Acme): Exported usage rows for r-9f3b window and uploaded to the support case. Noted weird double-charge on 2026-03-16 09:12 UTC.
Carmen (Eng): Creating internal bug: TOOL-4821 "gateway: use explicit call_id in result assembly". Will push hotfix branch, add unit + integration test for out-of-order router responses.
Elaine (QA): I'll add regression tests to catch this (simulate router out-of-order returns and assert mapping by call_id).
Alice (Support): Escalating to SEV-3 due to incorrect outputs + billing impact. Billing Ops pinged. Keeping customer updated. :rotating_light:
Dave (Acme): Thanks all. Appreciate the quick triage. We'll hold on reverting to sequential for now; waiting on your patch.
Carmen (Eng): I'll post PR link and canary timeline shortly. Thanks for the repro + trace header — that sped this up.
Alice (Support): Follow-ups: update thread when patch is canaried and when Billing reconciles.
deploy-bot: canary deploy paused at 1728130450 (auto-hold triggered by mapping anomalies).
